outcome: Enable deterministic video-frame perception beside the backend MCP tools and measure one model-driven DataSpace task_312 run.
criteria: An opt-in harness MCP reader inspects local videos and returns bounded timestamped image frames with saved source provenance, without a model or perception code in the backend.
Agent observations can be saved with frame references and explicit revisions, then imported through the existing backend tools; focused tests cover scope, evidence and host integration.

Verify image delivery through the configured OpenCode and model gateway with a synthetic visual probe, then run task_312 once and record its evidence, official verdict and limitations without task-specific extraction rules.

dispositions.note: Added an opt-in harness-only FFmpeg MCP reader with context confinement, bounded timestamped PNG responses, source/frame hashes and saved evidence; the backend is unchanged.

Observation JSON preserves cited frames and explicit supersedes/reason revisions and imports through Backend.import_dataset. Focused tests verify scope, image content, provenance, revisions and host permissions; 252 repository tests passed with one host-FFmpeg skip, and all five reader tests passed in the container including real decoding.

A synthetic random six-digit video probe passed through OpenCode 1.18.26 and the configured Qwen gateway. One task_312 run passed the official evaluator and scored 1.0 in the comparison scorer: 242 rows, three columns, 13 model steps, 12 tool calls, 69.8 seconds. Source/input manifests, raw image events, timestamps and the verdict are retained locally and documented.

note: Implemented generic video perception without benchmark extraction rules or a backend model. The passing task still skipped recording and importing its observation, amended its contract only after a dataset mismatch, sampled only through 50 seconds of a roughly 77.5-second video and did not transcribe audio. The measurement README and handoff preserve those limitations; the result establishes one correct answer and the image transport path, not general video readiness or compliance with the evidence/review protocol.
